max_rss_read_timing.meaning: Aggregate and detailed /proc reads occur at different instants. Their maxima are not asserted equal.

service_parent_device_discard_bytes.meaning: The parent group records substantial additional discard traffic not charged to the observed service group; no specific process or cause is identified.

service_socket_throttling_events.interpretation: This is the recorded sock_throttled counter of the service cgroup, not an identified Lean-PID event. No socket or process responsible is identified by these snapshots.

process_identity.scope_caution: The state is the leader state, not every thread state.

dio_activation.time_of_dio_readback: Immediately after enabling DIO before restoration; no later DIO readback is present.

limits: Different GitHub runners and unobserved background/cache/storage conditions prevent treating these two runs as a controlled same-host causal estimate.
The previous run did not include an effective-DIO flag readback; its unchanged setup did not explicitly request DIO.
Current runtime reports Linux 7.0.0-1017-azure. Earlier Linux 6.8 source reasoning is not a byte-bound description of this actual running kernel.
Process read_bytes and cgroup block-device counters are reported in their actual accounting scopes. Nested groups and stacked loop/backing devices must not be added as unique physical I/O.
Cgroup counters include other charged work; PSI cannot be added to CPU time as disjoint waiting time.
The visible cgroup mount root is not proof that no ancestor or external limit exists outside the cgroup namespace; root ENOENT interfaces remain unobservable.
Leader state S does not determine all worker-thread states; no per-thread wait channel, stack, syscall trace, mapped-file index or fault address was recorded.
Large VmSize or its growth does not prove a particular module was loaded or a deterministic mmap address collided.
No import, proof-body phase, mmap failure, supervisor policy or specific source file is identified as the cause.
This comparison neither creates nor authenticates an original kernel receipt or any family closure.

process_identity.scope_caution: The state is the leader state, not every thread state.

supported_observations: DIO was actually changed false/0 to true/1 on the same owned loop before restoration, with both native readbacks agreeing.
Both diagnostic copies timed out at 900 seconds without any persisted phase marker or Lean log bytes; there is no observed header-complete improvement.
The DIO run has lower service memory-PSI totals, fewer direct-reclaim scans and fewer service swap-in/swap-out counter increments.
The DIO run has higher process-attributed read_bytes, minor and major faults, file refaults, kswapd scans and system CPU; global SwapFree reaches zero.

At both readable non-root levels memory.max/high/swap.max remain 'max', cpu.max remains 'max 100000', and CPU throttle counters plus low/high/max/oom/oom_kill/oom_group_kill events remain zero. The DIO service has 151 sock_throttled events; all three visible levels retain zero proactive scan/steal counters.

In both runs rchar/syscr become constant around observer30s while page faults and read_bytes keep increasing. This is consistent with continuing paging activity but identifies no exact import or instruction.

VmSize in the DIO process ultimately reaches 113440182272 bytes at observer 702.60 s, versus 110218977280 bytes from observer 100.75 s in the previous process. This is virtual address-space growth, not a proved count of imported modules.
timing_method: All times are observer-relative. Counter deltas cover only the first through last valid identity-consistent Lean sample in each run; no startup/final interval extrapolation. Windows differ by 0.96 seconds.
